context:

2026-10-13 closeout: scripts/agent_write_preflight.sh strips one pair of matching surrounding single or double quotes (PR #2933, merge 499a6955a). description:
pre-commit writes INSTALL_PYTHON into the hook with shlex.quote. shlex.quote adds quotes only when the value has a character outside [\w@%+=:,./-]. So the quoting affects Windows interpreter paths (backslash, for example INSTALL_PYTHON='D:\a\BenchBox\...\python.exe') and POSIX interpreter paths with spaces or shell-special characters. It does not affect normal macOS or Linux agent writes.

scripts/agent_write_preflight.sh (about lines 175-179) takes the raw text after '=', quotes included, and tests it with [ ! -x ... ], so it reports 'shared pre-commit hook is not usable' for a quoted path. This is the Windows failure of tests/unit/test_agent_write_preflight.py::test_configured_hook_allows_linked_worktree_commit (line 195) in run 37967682464. Strip one pair of surrounding single quotes after reading the value (hook_interpreter=${hook_interpreter#\'}; hook_interpreter=${hook_interpreter%\'}), or unquote it with a shell-safe parse. This script gates every agent write on every platform, so test it with a quoted and an unquoted path and confirm on a Windows run that [ -x "D:\a\...\python.exe" ] passes under Git Bash. Later steps of that test may reveal more failures.

Put the new Linux quoted-path test in a new test file, not in tests/unit/test_agent_write_preflight.py. The existing file carries whole-file-digest comment-policy exceptions, and editing it triggers the two-PR flow described in comment-policy-digest-and-base-exception-catch22-20261008.
